title: Resilience Playbook: Compact GPU Pool Controls & Burst Tuning (UX prototype)
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Goal:
Design a compact, action-oriented GPU Pool Controls panel and an accompanying 'Resilience Playbook' that surface health signals, suggest safe burst/autoscale configurations, and provide one-click mitigation actions for on-call and SRE users. Target is a mobile-friendly, condensed UI card that fits inside the Dedicated Pool list and a full details canvas for power users.

Problem statement:
Operators currently have to switch between several console pages to understand pool health (latency, OOMs, throttling), cost impact, and to perform emergency actions (drain, scale, rollback). This increases time-to-mitigation and risk during incidents. We need a compact interaction surface that balances operator speed with safeguards to prevent accidental disruptive actions.

Design scope and proposals included in this prototype:
- Compact Pool Card (list view): health sparkline, 3-key metric badges (p95 latency, token throughput, active GPUs), a cost delta indicator, and a small 'Resilience' chevron to expand inline controls.
- Inline Quick Actions: safe-mode toggle, temporary burst slider (0-200% with cost-estimate tooltip), graceful-drain button (with confirmation + ETA), and an autoscale plan preview.
- Resilience Details Canvas: timeline of recent incidents, recommended emergency runbook steps, model-compatibility hints, and 'Apply suggestion' CTA to push settings to pool.
- Cost-aware defaults: the burst slider shows an estimated spend range computed from recent per-token costs; UI emphasizes low-risk presets (Safe, Conservative, Aggressive).
- Microcopy & confirmations: layered confirmations for destructive actions, justification notes required for admin overrides (audit trail for Private deployments).
- Accessibility: keyboard-first controls for quick action focus, ARIA labels for badge semantics, color contrast checks for health indicators.

Constraints & trade-offs:
- Engineering: real-time token-cost estimates require a short aggregation window; fallback is a cached estimate with a 'stale' indicator.
- Safety: emergency drain must be reversible but may trigger downstream job cancellations; design chooses a two-step reversible flow + optional 'force' checkbox for admins.
- Space: compact card must remain legible at narrow widths; chose iconography + abbreviated numbers over long labels.

Deliverables in this ticket:
- Figma prototype links (compact card, details canvas, confirmations)
- Design handoff file with tokens, interaction spec, and copy
- Acceptance criteria and test scenarios for PM/Eng verification

Acceptance criteria (must be testable):
1) Compact Pool Card renders in list view at 320px width without truncation of key metrics.
2) Burst slider shows estimated cost delta for current 10-minute window and updates when sliding.
3) Safe-mode toggle prevents new burst actions from being applied until manually disabled.
4) Emergency drain triggers the confirmation modal with required justification input and creates an audit note link.
5) Design tokens and annotations exported in handoff package; no missing color/spacing tokens.

Artifacts:
- Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/placeholder/Resilience-Playbook-Prototype
- Interactive prototype (Figma): https://www.figma.com/proto/placeholder/Resilience-Playbook
- Confluence spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Resilience+Playbook+Design
- Dev PR (stub): https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-console/pull/1729

Notes for engineering:
- Backend needs a new aggregated endpoint: /pools/{id}/resilience-preview that returns recent health aggregates and cost estimates; if realtime not available, allow a cached/last-known object with a timestamp.
- Autoscale suggestions are UI-first: initial implementation can post as a suggested config in the Console, not auto-apply.

Success metrics (for rollout):
- Reduction in mean-time-to-first-action for incidents on Dedicated pools by 20% within 6 weeks of rollout.
- 30% of bursts initiated through compact controls use 'Safe' preset.
- No accidental emergency drains during pilot (tracked via audit logs).
